careers.title: Electrician
careers.description: Install, maintain, and repair electrical systems in homes, businesses, and job sites.

startup.description: At a small electrical contractor, you wear every hat and handle jobs end to end.
pros: Learn fast, close to the owner

mid.description: A regional contractor gives you steady crews and bigger commercial projects.

enterprise.description: At a large industrial or utility employer, you specialize and work to tight standards.

entry.note: Most electricians start as apprentices and earn while they learn under a licensed journeyman.

proofProjects.title: Home lab wiring board
proofProjects.brief: Build a practice panel with outlets, switches, and GFCI. Photo the layout and walk through your safety checklist.

proofProjects.title: Code-compliant lighting plan
proofProjects.brief: Draft a one-room lighting plan with circuit loads and a materials list that matches local code basics.

careers.title: Chef / Cook
careers.description: Create dishes and run the line in kitchens, from cafes to fine dining.

startup.description: In a small indie kitchen you own the menu and cook what you believe in.

mid.description: A growing restaurant group offers structure and a real brigade.
pros: Chance to lead a station or kitchen

enterprise.description: Hotels and large operators need chefs who can scale quality to volume.

entry.note: Culinary school helps, but many chefs climb from prep cook with a strong station portfolio and stage experience.

proofProjects.title: Three-course tasting menu
proofProjects.brief: Cook and plate a full tasting for guests. Document mise, timing, and cost per plate.

proofProjects.title: Station run book
proofProjects.brief: Write a one-page run book for a station you know: setup, ticket flow, and close-down.

careers.title: Carpenter / Builder
careers.description: Build and finish structures and furniture from wood and other materials.

startup.description: As a solo or small-crew carpenter you take custom jobs start to finish.

mid.description: A construction firm offers bigger projects and a dependable crew.

enterprise.description: Large developers run high-volume, spec-driven builds.

entry.note: Trade school or an apprenticeship is the usual door. A clean project portfolio beats a resume alone.

proofProjects.title: Built-in shelf install
proofProjects.brief: Design, cut, and install a small built-in. Show measurements, joinery, and finish.

proofProjects.title: Framing detail study
proofProjects.brief: Rebuild a common framing detail (header, stair stringer) and label every member.

careers.title: Data Analyst
careers.description: Turn messy data into clear insights that help people make decisions.

startup.description: You're the whole data team - set up tracking and answer everything.

mid.description: A scaling company gives you cleaner data and a small analytics team.

enterprise.description: Big companies have mature data platforms and deep specialization.

entry.note: A degree helps, but hiring managers often care more about SQL, clear dashboards, and a public analysis repo.

proofProjects.title: Public data deep dive
proofProjects.brief: Pick an open dataset, ask a real business question, and ship a dashboard plus a one-page insight memo.

proofProjects.title: Metric definition kit
proofProjects.brief: Define 5 product metrics with SQL, edge cases, and a short glossary teammates can reuse.

careers.title: Software Engineer
careers.description: Design and build the apps, sites, and systems people use every day.

startup.description: You ship fast across the whole stack and see your code reach users instantly.

mid.description: A growth-stage company balances speed with real engineering practices.

enterprise.description: Large tech companies offer deep specialization and polished systems.

entry.note: CS degrees still help, but shipped projects with READMEs, tests, and a live demo open many doors.

proofProjects.title: Full-stack product slice
proofProjects.brief: Ship one real feature end to end: auth, data model, API, and UI. Deploy it and write the tradeoffs.

proofProjects.title: System design writeup
proofProjects.brief: Document how you would scale a simple app. Diagrams, bottlenecks, and what you would cut first.

careers.title: Research Scientist
careers.description: Run experiments and investigations to push knowledge forward.

startup.description: At a research startup you chase a focused breakthrough with a tight team.

mid.description: A mid-size lab or institute balances exploration with resources.

enterprise.description: Big R&D orgs fund long-horizon research with serious infrastructure.

entry.note: Most research scientist roles expect a graduate degree and a publication or thesis trail.

proofProjects.title: Replication study
proofProjects.brief: Reproduce a published experiment on public data. Share methods, results, and where you diverged.

proofProjects.title: Lit review brief
proofProjects.brief: Write a tight review of 8 to 12 papers on one question with a clear open problem at the end.

careers.title: Graphic Designer
careers.description: Craft visuals, brands, and layouts that communicate and delight.

startup.description: You shape the whole brand and touch everything visual.

mid.description: A growing brand team gives you focus and real projects.

enterprise.description: Large companies have polished brand systems and specialized roles.

entry.note: Portfolios win. Formal school is optional if your case studies show craft and client thinking.

proofProjects.title: Brand system mini
proofProjects.brief: Create a logo, type, color, and 3 mock applications for a fictional or local business.

proofProjects.title: Campaign case study
proofProjects.brief: Redesign a campaign end to end and explain constraints, options you killed, and final rationale.

careers.title: Video / Content Creator
careers.description: Plan, shoot, and edit video and content that builds an audience.

startup.description: Solo or tiny team - you're writer, shooter, and editor all at once.

mid.description: A brand or agency gives you gear, budget, and a small crew.

enterprise.description: Large media teams produce polished content at scale.

entry.note: Audience and published work matter more than credentials. Consistency and analytics literacy help.

proofProjects.title: Series of 6
proofProjects.brief: Ship a tight content series on one topic. Track what performed and rewrite one piece from the data.

proofProjects.title: Format experiment
proofProjects.brief: Test two formats for the same idea. Document hooks, retention notes, and what you would scale.

careers.title: UX / Product Designer
careers.description: Design how apps and products look, feel, and work for real people.

startup.description: You own the whole product experience and ship designs fast.

mid.description: A growing product team lets you focus and build a design system.

enterprise.description: Big companies have mature design orgs and deep research.

entry.note: Strong case studies beat degrees. Show research, flows, and shipped outcomes when you can.

proofProjects.title: End-to-end case study
proofProjects.brief: Problem, research, wireframes, UI, and what changed after feedback. Keep it honest about constraints.

proofProjects.title: AI feature redesign
proofProjects.brief: Redesign an AI-assisted flow with clear empty states, trust cues, and failure handling.

careers.title: Registered Nurse
careers.description: Care for patients, deliver treatments, and be their advocate.

startup.description: Clinics and small practices offer close patient relationships.

mid.description: Community hospitals balance variety with support.

enterprise.description: Large hospital systems offer specialties and advancement.

entry.note: Licensed nursing requires an accredited program and board exams. There is no portfolio shortcut.

proofProjects.title: Clinical skills checklist
proofProjects.brief: Build a personal skills log from clinicals or simulation: procedure, confidence, and what to practice next.

proofProjects.title: Patient education one-pager
proofProjects.brief: Write a clear handout for a common condition at a 6th-grade reading level and get peer feedback.

careers.title: Teacher / Educator
careers.description: Help people learn, grow, and discover what they're capable of.

startup.description: Small or charter schools let you shape your own classroom style.

mid.description: A typical public school offers structure and a full staff.

enterprise.description: Large districts and ed-tech orgs offer scale and specialization.

entry.note: Public school teaching usually needs a credential. Tutoring and curriculum samples can help you get started earlier.

proofProjects.title: Unit plan sample
proofProjects.brief: Design a 2-week unit with objectives, lessons, and assessments you could actually teach.

proofProjects.title: Classroom demo lesson
proofProjects.brief: Record or write a full lesson with pacing, checks for understanding, and differentiation notes.

careers.title: Counselor / Therapist
careers.description: Support people's mental health and help them work through challenges.

startup.description: Private practice means you choose your clients and approach.

mid.description: Group practices and clinics provide referrals and peers.

enterprise.description: Hospitals and health systems offer stability and specialties.

entry.note: Licensed counseling requires graduate training and supervised hours. Peer support roles can be a step earlier.

proofProjects.title: Resource map
proofProjects.brief: Build a local resource guide for a population you care about with clear next steps and warm handoffs.

proofProjects.title: Session structure template
proofProjects.brief: Draft a first-session outline with intake questions, goals, and notes on boundaries and referrals.

careers.title: Product Manager
careers.description: Decide what to build and lead the team to ship it.

startup.description: You set the vision and do a bit of everything to ship it.

mid.description: A growth company gives you a focused product area and a team.

enterprise.description: Big companies need PMs to align many teams on one product.

entry.note: PMs come from engineering, design, support, and ops. Show judgment with PRDs and shipped experiments.

proofProjects.title: One-page PRD
proofProjects.brief: Write a PRD for a real product gap: problem, users, success metrics, and a cut-line for v1.

proofProjects.title: Opportunity brief
proofProjects.brief: Size a problem with public data or user interviews. Recommend ship, iterate, or kill.

careers.title: Marketing Manager
careers.description: Grow an audience and get the right people to care about a product.

startup.description: You run all of marketing and test everything to find what works.

mid.description: A scaling company gives you a channel to own and a small team.

enterprise.description: Large brands run coordinated, big-budget marketing programs.

entry.note: Degrees help at big brands; startups hire for campaigns you can prove with numbers and creative samples.

proofProjects.title: Campaign teardown
proofProjects.brief: Analyze a live campaign: funnel, creative, spend assumptions, and three changes you would try next.

proofProjects.title: Launch plan
proofProjects.brief: Write a 30-day launch plan for a product with channels, assets, and how you will measure lift.

careers.title: Account Executive (Sales)
careers.description: Build relationships and close deals that grow the business.

startup.description: You're an early rep, figuring out the pitch and closing founding customers.

mid.description: A growing company gives you leads, a process, and a quota.

enterprise.description: Large companies run big, complex deals with full support.

entry.note: Sales is proof-heavy. Pipeline stories, call recordings, and quota history beat formal schooling.

proofProjects.title: Outbound sequence
proofProjects.brief: Build a 7-touch sequence with talk tracks, objection handling, and a simple CRM tracker.

proofProjects.title: Discovery call script
proofProjects.brief: Write and practice a discovery call that surfaces pain, budget, and next step without pitching early.

careers.title: Accountant
careers.description: Keep finances accurate, organized, and compliant.

startup.description: You handle the whole set of books and learn every part of finance.

mid.description: A finance team lets you focus on an area and grow.

enterprise.description: Large companies have specialized teams and strong systems.

entry.note: Accounting roles usually expect a degree; CPA tracks add more school and exams. Bookkeeping can start earlier.

proofProjects.title: Books for a small biz
proofProjects.brief: Set up a chart of accounts and monthly close checklist for a fictional shop. Export clean reports.

proofProjects.title: Variance analysis memo
proofProjects.brief: Explain a budget vs actual gap in plain language with drivers and recommended actions.

careers.title: Project Manager
careers.description: Keep projects, people, and deadlines moving in the right direction.

startup.description: You bring order to a fast, scrappy team juggling many things.

mid.description: A growing company gives you defined projects and processes.

enterprise.description: Large orgs run complex programs across many stakeholders.

entry.note: Coordinators often grow from ops or admin. Certifications help; calm delivery and clear trackers matter more.

proofProjects.title: Project tracker kit
proofProjects.brief: Build a lightweight tracker with owners, risks, and a weekly status template teams can reuse.

proofProjects.title: Retro writeup
proofProjects.brief: Run a mock retrospective on a delayed project. Capture what happened and three process changes.

careers.title: Operations Analyst
careers.description: Make how a business runs smoother, cheaper, and more reliable.

startup.description: You design the systems a young company needs to scale.

mid.description: A scaling company needs you to tighten and standardize operations.

enterprise.description: Large companies optimize operations at serious scale.

entry.note: Ops analysts mix data and process. Spreadsheets, SOPs, and a before/after workflow story go far.

proofProjects.title: Process map + fix
proofProjects.brief: Map a messy process, find the bottleneck, and propose a simpler flow with a KPI to watch.

proofProjects.title: Ops dashboard
proofProjects.brief: Build a weekly ops dashboard from sample data with alerts for when something is off.

careers.title: Design Engineer
careers.description: Ship product UI yourself: design systems, prototypes, and production front-end in one seat.

entry.note: Hiring is portfolio-first. Show design craft and code that shipped, not just mockups.

proofProjects.title: Designed and shipped feature
proofProjects.brief: Own a feature from sketch to production PR. Include before/after and accessibility notes.

proofProjects.title: Tiny design system
proofProjects.brief: Build 8 to 12 reusable components with tokens, states, and a living docs page.

proofProjects.title: Prototype that became code
proofProjects.brief: Take a fuzzy product idea to interactive prototype, then implement the core path yourself.

startup.description: You are often the design and front-end team. Speed and taste matter more than process.

mid.description: You partner with PMs and backend while owning web surfaces end to end.

enterprise.description: You work inside mature systems and stricter accessibility and brand rules.

careers.title: ML Engineer
careers.description: Put models into production: training pipelines, evaluation, serving, and monitoring.

entry.note: Strong degrees help, but deployed systems with evals and metrics can beat credentials alone.

proofProjects.title: RAG assistant with evals
proofProjects.brief: Ship retrieval + answers with citation and a small evaluation suite for quality and cost.

proofProjects.title: Training to serving path
proofProjects.brief: Train a model, containerize inference, and log latency plus failure modes.

proofProjects.title: Data pipeline for features
proofProjects.brief: Build a reproducible feature pipeline with validation checks and a clear schema.

startup.description: You wear research and production hats. Pragmatism beats perfect papers.

mid.description: Clearer ownership of a model area with platform support starting to exist.

enterprise.description: Mature platforms, compliance, and specialization around a model family.

careers.title: AI Product Manager
careers.description: Decide where AI helps users: define problems, eval criteria, and ship features that stay trustworthy.

entry.note: Often grows from PM, eng, or research. Show AI judgment with PRDs and eval frameworks, not buzzwords.

proofProjects.title: AI feature PRD
proofProjects.brief: Write a PRD with user jobs, failure modes, eval metrics, and a human-in-the-loop plan.

proofProjects.title: Eval scorecard
proofProjects.brief: Define how you know the model is good enough: quality, safety, cost, and latency thresholds.

proofProjects.title: Opportunity teardown
proofProjects.brief: Pick a product and argue where AI should not ship yet. Clarity about cuts is the skill.

startup.description: You invent the AI roadmap while sitting with founders and eng.

mid.description: You own a slice of AI surface area with clearer teams around you.

enterprise.description: Governance, risk, and platform teams shape what you can ship.

careers.title: AI Ops Engineer
careers.description: Keep AI systems reliable in production: prompts, tools, evals, cost, and incident response.

entry.note: Newer role. Prove you can run eval harnesses, reduce cost, and debug flaky model behavior.

proofProjects.title: Eval harness
proofProjects.brief: Build a regression suite for prompts or agents with golden cases and a weekly score report.

proofProjects.title: Cost and latency dashboard
proofProjects.brief: Instrument an LLM path and show how you cut spend without tanking quality.

proofProjects.title: Incident playbook
proofProjects.brief: Write a runbook for model drift or tool failures with rollback steps and owners.

startup.description: You invent the ops layer while features keep changing under you.

mid.description: Dedicated ownership of AI reliability as product volume grows.

enterprise.description: Heavy process, audits, and shared platforms for many AI products.

careers.title: Prompt & Eval Engineer
careers.description: Design prompts, tools, and evaluation suites so AI features behave predictably.

entry.note: Still forming as a title. Strong writing, systematic evals, and public case studies matter most.

proofProjects.title: Prompt library with versions
proofProjects.brief: Ship versioned prompts for one use case with before/after quality notes.

proofProjects.title: Human eval rubric
proofProjects.brief: Create a rubric raters can use consistently and measure agreement on 50 examples.

proofProjects.title: Failure gallery
proofProjects.brief: Catalog model failures by type and the prompt or tool change that fixed each class.

startup.description: You sit next to product and ship prompt changes fast.

mid.description: More structure: datasets, raters, and shared eval platforms.

enterprise.description: Eval rigor and documentation become part of risk and brand trust.

careers.title: AI Product Designer
careers.description: Design interfaces for generative and agentic products: trust, control, and recovery when models miss.

entry.note: Case studies that show AI-specific UX (uncertainty, edits, citations) beat generic UI galleries.

proofProjects.title: AI flow case study
proofProjects.brief: Design a generative flow with loading, partial results, edit, and undo. Explain trust choices.

proofProjects.title: Error and empty states kit
proofProjects.brief: Design a kit for hallucinations, refusals, and offline modes that still feels on-brand.

proofProjects.title: Human-in-the-loop review UI
proofProjects.brief: Prototype a review queue where people correct model output and feed improvements back.

startup.description: You invent patterns while the model still changes weekly.

mid.description: You refine AI surfaces with stronger research and design system support.

enterprise.description: Accessibility, brand, and risk review shape every generative surface.

careers.title: Model Maker
careers.description: Make working metal or plastic models and prototypes on machines like lathes, mills, and CNC. Real BLS/O*NET title: Model Makers, Metal and Plastic (51-4061).

entry.note: O*NET: typically high school plus moderate-term on-the-job training or apprenticeship. CNC and blueprint skill show up in the job tasks.

proofProjects.title: Prototype from a print
proofProjects.brief: Make a working model from a blueprint or CAD file. Show tolerances, tools used, and what you reworked.

proofProjects.title: Jig or fixture
proofProjects.brief: Build a jig or fixture that improves a repeat cut or assembly, as listed in O*NET tasks for this occupation.

startup.description: A small product shop or inventing team needs one-off models fast, often with limited machines.

mid.description: A manufacturer or product company with a model shop supporting engineering.

enterprise.description: Auto, aerospace, or appliance model shops with formal process and inspection.

careers.title: Industrial Designer
careers.description: Shape physical products: form, materials, and how something feels in the hand.

entry.note: A degree helps at big brands; a physical + digital portfolio of objects you designed often matters more.

proofProjects.title: Object redesign
proofProjects.brief: Pick an everyday object, redesign it, and show sketches, model, and a rough prototype.

proofProjects.title: Materials study
proofProjects.brief: Make the same form in two materials and document feel, cost, and manufacturing notes.

proofProjects.title: Case study deck
proofProjects.brief: Tell the story of one product: problem, users, iterations, and final rationale.

startup.description: You invent form while engineering is still catching up.

mid.description: Clearer product cycles with engineers and marketers in the loop.

enterprise.description: Brand systems, tooling constraints, and long product cycles.

careers.title: Warehouse Ops Lead
careers.description: Run the floor: people, flow, safety, and throughput in warehouses and fulfillment.

entry.note: Many leads grow from the floor. Supervisory proof and process improvements beat a classroom alone.

proofProjects.title: Flow map
proofProjects.brief: Map a pick/pack flow, find the bottleneck, and propose a change with a simple metric.

proofProjects.title: Shift checklist
proofProjects.brief: Write a start/mid/end shift checklist that a new hire could follow on day one.

startup.description: Small warehouse or 3PL cell where you invent process as you go.

mid.description: Regional site with KPIs, leads, and clearer ladders.

enterprise.description: Large fulfillment network with WMS and strict SOPs.

careers.title: Electrical Engineer
careers.description: Design, develop, and test electrical systems and equipment - power, electronics, controls. BLS/O*NET 17-2071.

entry.note: O*NET: typically a bachelor's in electrical engineering. Licensure (PE) matters for some public and consulting roles.

proofProjects.title: Circuit or control project
proofProjects.brief: Design and document a circuit or control system with requirements, schematic, and test results.

proofProjects.title: System analysis writeup
proofProjects.brief: Analyze a power or electronics problem with calculations, tradeoffs, and a recommended design path.

startup.description: Small hardware or energy teams need generalists who design and debug end to end.

mid.description: Product or industrial firms with clearer systems and design reviews.

enterprise.description: Utilities, aerospace, semiconductor, or large electronics with heavy process.
